official.deadline_note: No fixed closing date is published. The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for internships continuing into 2026 are closed; a budget will be available again in 2027 and applications for internships taking place in 2027 reopen from January 2027. Inside a funded budget year you may apply up to six months in advance until one day before the internship starts.
official.status_note: The programme page carries a clear notice: 'No more grants for 2026. You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: The grant is a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, consisting of a one-off travel allowance and an expense allowance for accommodation and living expenses; no tuition or course fees are covered.
benefits: One-off payment of 200 EUR for travel expenses if the internship is within Europe (all Council of Europe member states, Belarus and Kosovo).
One-off payment of 500 EUR for travel expenses if the internship is located outside Europe.
No reimbursement of travel expenses if the internship is in Belgium.
Monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, set annually and multiplied by the number of months the internship is active, varying by host city.
Payment in two instalments: 85% of the total grant after approval, and the remaining 15% after the internship once the internship report and the supervisor's evaluation report are submitted.
The grant is not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, so it is not an obstacle to the Flemish Growth Package or child benefit.
eligibility: You are younger than 35 on the start date of your internship.
You have obtained a secondary or higher education diploma in Flanders; nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant.
You have secured an internship with a multilateral organisation from the published qualifying list.
The internship lasts at least two and up to six months.
The internship must take place at the headquarters or a field office of the organisation, within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
requirements: Hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution.
Have secured the internship; you may apply up to six months before it starts or after it has started.
Your internship supervisor must complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
If you apply after the internship has started, the remaining period counted from the first day after you submit must be at least two months.
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and have your supervisor complete and submit the evaluation form, at the latest two months after the end of the internship.
Take part in an intake interview before the internship and a follow-up conversation afterwards.
documents: Diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution.
Letter of acceptance from the organisation, or another certificate proving that you have been accepted for the internship.
Attestation regarding the internship offer, completed by your internship supervisor and submitted to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
Personal evaluation form, completed by you.
Evaluation form completed by your internship supervisor and submitted to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
Internship report, required for the second instalment.
Extension certificate, only if you extend the internship.
selection_criteria: No competitive jury or published ranking is described; the published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme.
An application is only processed while budget is available; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available.
The average administrative lead time for a grant application is three weeks.
coverage: One-off payment of 200 EUR (Europe) or 500 EUR (outside Europe) for travel expenses.
Monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, set annually and multiplied by the number of active internship months, varying by host city.

Published monthly amounts range from 1,047.60 EUR (Lilongwe) to 2,721.97 EUR (Geneva), with 1,669.92 EUR for Antwerp, Bruges, Brussels and Luxembourg, 1,903.70 EUR for Barcelona and 2,037.30 EUR for Paris and Washington D.C.
No travel reimbursement for an internship in Belgium.
application_method: Check you meet the eligibility conditions, in particular the age and Flemish diploma requirements.
Secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation, either through a vacancy published on the programme's internships page or by a spontaneous application.
Submit the online application form with the required documents.
Have your internship supervisor complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
Receive approval once all documents are provided and the requirements are met, then take part in the intake interview.
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and the supervisor's evaluation form within two months and take part in the follow-up conversation.
official.application_route: Submit the online application form on the programme page with the diploma, acceptance and identity documents, plus the supervisor's attestation sent to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant; you must hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders.
official.international_eligibility: Any nationality is eligible provided the diploma was obtained at a Flemish educational institution.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The internship must be with a multilateral organisation on the published qualifying list, at its headquarters or a field office within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
official.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months; the internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
official.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme offers young global citizens financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation, aimed at people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The grant is a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly allowance for accommodation and living expenses.

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single value - the Government of Flanders publishes the living allowance as a city-by-city monthly matrix (1,047.60 to 2,721.97 EUR) plus a one-off travel payment of 200 or 500 EUR, so no single award figure exists
funding_period - the allowance is an annually set monthly amount multiplied by active internship months, so a single cadence is not published
english_requirement - the published pages state no English or language requirement
deadline_central - no closing date is published; the scheme is budget-limited and reopens in January 2027
verification.notes: The programme page and its dedicated 'Grant amounts' page were read in full on the awarding body's own domain (vlaanderen.be). The 200/500 EUR travel payments, the full city matrix of monthly living amounts, the two-instalment 85/15 payment split and the three-week average lead time were all confirmed there.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a reimbursement scheme, not a scholarship competition: there is no jury, and you only get a grant while annual budget lasts, which is why the 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2027 internships reopen from January 2027. The money is a one-off travel payment of 200 or 500 EUR plus a monthly living allowance that depends entirely on your host city, so check the published matrix before you accept a placement - Geneva pays roughly two and a half times Lilongwe. It also does not touch tuition, and the grant is reduced by any remuneration or allowance you receive for the same internship from another government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Anyone under 35 with a diploma from a Flemish institution who has already secured, or is about to secure, an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the published city matrix for your host city before committing - the monthly amount varies from about 1,048 to 2,722 EUR.

Confirm your host organisation appears on the qualifying multilateral organisations list and that the placement is at an HQ or field office inside the jurisdiction of Flanders' diplomatic representations.
Ask your supervisor early for the attestation regarding the internship offer, which they must send to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
Time the application to the budget year: apply from January 2027 for a 2027 internship, up to six months in advance.
If the internship has already started, check that at least two months remain after your submission date.
Diarise the post-internship obligations: your personal evaluation form and the supervisor's evaluation form within two months, plus the internship report that unlocks the final 15%.
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the annual budget is exhausted - the application is not processed and is not held over.
An internship shorter than two months, or a remaining period of less than two months if you apply after it has started.
A host that is not on the published qualifying list of multilateral organisations.
Holding a foreign diploma rather than one obtained at a Flemish educational institution.
Turning 35 before the internship start date.
Receiving a salary or allowance for the same internship from another body without declaring it, which reduces the grant.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and course fees are not covered, and there is no travel payment at all for an internship in Belgium. Anything above the fixed travel payment and the city-based monthly allowance - visa costs, insurance, relocation, flights above the lump sum - comes out of your own pocket.
document_audit: The supervisor's attestation is sent by the supervisor, not uploaded by you, so build in chase time.
The personal evaluation form must be completed by you; the supervisor's evaluation form is separate and also goes to the programme mailbox.
The internship report is what triggers the second instalment, so an unfinished report means 15% of the grant stays unpaid.
An extension certificate is needed if you extend the internship - and the extension limit is six months, or nine for a Flanders-funded project.
alerts: The 2026 budget is exhausted; applications for internships taking place in 2027 reopen from January 2027.
The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.

Keep the Growth Package: the grant is not a salary, so it does not block the Flemish Growth Package or child benefit for 12 months after you finish studying, provided you are under 25 and take no salary from the host.
Average administrative turnaround is three weeks, but an application submitted once the budget is gone is not kept for the next round.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You secure the internship, file the online application with your diploma, acceptance and identity documents, your supervisor sends the attestation to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be, the programme approves while budget lasts, pays 85% up front and the remaining 15% after your report and evaluation forms are in, with an intake interview before and a follow-up conversation after.
